title: Bench-top dial gauge and timer with metal sample and tubing on laboratory bench
objects_and_counts: No people are visible in the image.
One vertical dial gauge (round face) mounted on a blue vertical support is visible near the image centre; the gauge face has a needle and markings and a small central label showing "W's".
One metallic probe/nozzle is positioned directly under the dial gauge and points to a small cylindrical sample resting on a clear rectangular platform in the foreground centre.
One small cylindrical sample (light-coloured, about the diameter of the probe tip) is visible on the clear platform beneath the probe; the sample top appears darkened or dirty.
One small rectangular control box with front-panel indicators is visible front-centre-left; the front panel shows two green push-buttons or indicator holes and one red illuminated lamp.

Two distinct metal cylindrical vessels are visible on the bench: one shiny metal cup on the left on a square metal base, and one larger, taller rust-stained metal cylinder on the right (both are partially cropped at top/bottom).

At least three flexible tubes/hoses are visible (one transparent hose running from the probe to the right, one thicker transparent/cream hose curving behind the gauge, and additional white/transparent tubing coiled behind the bench); exact total count cannot be precisely determined due to overlap and partial occlusion.
One red plastic bucket is visible at the far left edge of the bench.
One blue plastic funnel or bowl is visible behind the centre area, partially obscured by hoses.

Two blue vertical equipment housings or panels are visible in the background left and right edges; each contains printed diagrams or markings and circular gauge cutouts (background panels are partially cropped).
